checks: Every generator is affine in the same vertical direction, including the two stationary ones. The fixed segment at first coordinate −1 and any right generator at first coordinate 1 are noncollinear, so the hull has area even at the collision.

The same square occurs at both endpoints. Opposing through-point halfplanes have total normalized area one because the common boundary is null; at the center each has mass one half by central symmetry.

At t=1/2 the two right vertices coincide at (1,0); the two fixed vertices and this one are a nondegenerate triangle, so the simplex depth formula gives 4/9. This is strictly below both endpoint values.

dependencies.hypotheses: The midpoint hull is a full-dimensional compact planar simplex. The simplex direction of the accepted equivalence gives normalized maximal ordinary depth (2/3)^2=4/9 for it.

overlap.comparison: The accepted failure of quasiconcavity concerns compatible interval fibers and ambient mixed length. It does not provide an ordinary planar full-dimensional four-generator shadow system.
It supplies the midpoint's depth, not the common-direction vertex path or comparison with its endpoint hulls.

readability: The proof and its scope are clear.
review_method: Independent proof read, source-scope and graph dependency checks, and exact arithmetic where applicable

sources_verified.scope_verified: Section 1 is the displayed continuous moving-vertex construction and its exact depths. Section 2 uses a separate fixed-integer interval construction outside this proof.

summary: The affine motion is a full-dimensional shadow system, and the square and midpoint triangle give the exact normalized ordinary depths claimed.
